MA-onboarding-redesign · Gate 1

Onboarding Redesign — Reconstructed Mockup

The original approved reference HTML (onboarding-final-approval-v5.html) no longer exists — it lived under the retired .superpowers/ session harness and was never committed. This mockup is rebuilt from the surviving 682-line locked spec (docs/scopes/MA-onboarding-redesign/assets/locked-design-2026-07-23.md), approved 2026-07-23. Where the prose underdetermined a visual choice, the call is made here and flagged in the report, not silently guessed.

Shell contract, visible in every frame below: one fixed header track (56px), one fixed 4-segment progress rail, a scrollable content viewport, and one always-mounted footer CTA track (52px). The blank strip directly above every footer is the reserved status track — it holds zero height of visible content on the idle/populated frames and only renders copy on the error frames. That's the "zero-shift" contract from the spec: state changes recolor or fill a slot that was already there, they never insert one.

N1 has no true empty state (it's static welcome content on every load) and N4 has no true empty state either — N3's business rule (≥1 account before N2 can be left) guarantees N4 always has data. The closest analogue for N4 is the "Exchange rate needed" fallback, included below. N3's empty state is explicitly unreachable through valid flow per the spec — its frame shows the redirect-to-N2 behavior instead of a broken success screen.

More Accounts Recovered (0 accounts)

Setting up your first account…

A resumed N3 with zero accounts never renders a broken success screen — the route resolver redirects straight to First Account before N3's content ever mounts. This is the only visual for N3's "empty" case; the spec explicitly forbids showing N3 itself with no accounts.
